messages:
maria: seeing a big spike of internal 502s in model-service over the last 6 mins, app logs showing a lot of 'i/o timeout' on DNS lookups. Started around 17:31 UTC. anyone else seeing DNS errors?

jonathan: yup, autoscaler logs show repeated failed lookups to metadata.service.local and kubelet is logging resolve timeouts too. correlation with a network change earlier?

infra-bot: alert triggered: dns-resolution-errors > threshold (svc:model-service) at 1751239876

sam: grabbed a tcpdump from one affected pod -> lots of UDP fragmentation and retransmits. snippet:
```
17:31:15.123456 IP 10.10.2.45.56234 > 10.1.2.3.53: UDP, length 1452
17:31:15.123457 IP 10.1.2.3.53 > 10.10.2.45.56234: UDP, length 1400
17:31:15.123458 IP (frag 1)
... IP reassembly failed
```

lisa: remember we rolled a Calico MTU change to 1442 in us-west about 2 hours ago (was 9000 before) as part of the pod-network tuning. Could be fragmentation hitting UDP DNS packets. Also some nodes have RDMA interfaces (ib0) that need consistent MTU.

kevin: coreDNS logs show a ton of: `read udp 10.1.2.3:53: i/o timeout`. EDNS advertised payload size is 1232 on our forwarders — that would cause larger UDP packets and fragmentation if MTU is low.

maria: node-local dns proxies are falling back to TCP a lot which is blowing up conntrack entries. seeing hundreds of short-lived TCP dns sessions per node.

jonathan: conntrack on a few nodes is near capacity. run: `sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max` -> 262144. conntrack shows many ESTABLISHED dns TCP entries from kube-proxy. that's killing new connections when table hits limit.

sam: quick mitigation: lower EDNS UDP size in CoreDNS forward plugin to 512 so responses fit under MTU, and limit EDNS to avoid fragmentation. can patch corefile quickly:
```
.:53 {
  forward . 10.1.2.3 {
    policy sequential
    max_fails 2
    tls_off
    proxy_no_edns
    edns_client_subnet 0
    edns_size 512
  }
  cache 30
}
```

lisa: rolling back the Calico MTU change on the canary pool now (us-west-canary). if that fixes it we should revert cluster-wide.

kevin: long term action items: ensure MTU consistency across eth/ib interfaces, add an MTU gating check to our rollout playbook, tune conntrack (nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_time_wait and nf_conntrack_max), and review CoreDNS EDNS defaults. Opening INF-1234.

maria: creating incident INF-1234 and paging on-call. if rollback doesn't stabilize we'll temporarily route dns to regional coredns replicas and drain affected GPU nodes to limit impact on latency-sensitive model traffic.

infra-bot: incident created INF-1234 by maria; severity: P1; responders: @oncall

sam: update 1751241620: rollback succeeded on 6/8 canary nodes ~2m ago, DNS timeouts dropped ~90% on those nodes, overall error rate for model-service decreased from 8% -> 0.8%. still watching for remaining two nodes and conntrack cleanup.

maria: thanks everyone. follow-ups: INF-1234 assigned to kevin for postmortem and a runbook for MTU/EDNS checks; sam will prepare CoreDNS quick-rollback patch; lisa will validate RDMA node configs.

kevin: putting a note — we should also test with `dig +bufsize=512` and tcpdump to confirm fragments are gone before closing incident.

maria: noted, closing updates once canary fully stable. :thumbsup:
